trust_decision.summary: Whether a request reached the local media server from a local origin: decided inside handle_request() by lower-casing the Host header and requiring it to start with one of 127.0.0.1:, localhost: or [::1]: (unless ANKI_API_HOST is 0.0.0.0), plus an Origin check when an Origin header is present; the published fix only renames the generator's loop variable and leaves this decision, and the tuple it builds, unchanged.

landing_point.why: The advisory summary is about the local HTTP server not validating requests, and every path except /favicon.ico enters through this one Flask catch-all route, where the Host/Origin gate is written.

fix_sites.module_kind: http_handler (request validation in the desktop app's local media server)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The only route outside the gate, /favicon.ico, returns one fixed bundled image with no path parameter and no user data, so a solver can call it an asset route the request-validation property was never meant to cover.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Deliberately non-browser and remote-API use: ANKI_API_HOST=0.0.0.0 switches the whole Host/Origin gate off, and a Bearer-token request is treated as having full API access; a fix that enforced Origin/Host unconditionally would break the CLI/API clients and the documented remote-API mode.

O6_input_shapes: Host value in mixed case (lower-cased before comparison)

O7_producer.where: The checked values are raw Host and Origin request headers supplied by the HTTP client; no schema, serializer, cache or config loader in the project produces them

O8_uncovered_routes.route: GET /favicon.ico is served by its own Flask rule that reads a bundled data file without passing the Host/Origin gate in handle_request
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Constant asset: the path is hard-coded to imgs/favicon.ico and the response is a public image, so nothing attacker-chosen is read and no user data is exposed.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, 0 packages, 157 lines above the landing point

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A further route function that serves files directly instead of going through handle_request
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: A maintainer adding a cheap static route registers it next to favicon(), and the gate only exists inside the catch-all, so it is easy to bypass.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second request gate (_check_dynamic_request_permissions) that enforces content-type and the API key but never the Host/Origin allow-list
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The module already carries two request gates; whoever added the content-type/key gate modeled a separate concern and left the host/origin check only in the catch-all, so a new endpoint class can land under the wrong gate.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A new dynamic GET handler added to _extract_dynamic_get_request
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: GET handlers return before the content-type and API-key checks, so a newly added one inherits only whatever the catch-all does.

O9_family: request origin/host validation (CWE-346), with path-traversal protection (CWE-22) growing in the same module

O10_build.language: Python 3 (qt/aqt) on top of a Rust core
O10_build.toolchain: uv workspace (root pyproject.toml, qt/pyproject.toml), cargo/ninja for the anki Rust backend, PyQt6 + PyQt6-WebEngine; pytest from the dev dependency group
O10_build.project_tests: qt/tests/test_mediasrv.py unit-tests ensure_safe_path and is_localhost_origin only; no test drives handle_request, the Host/Origin gate or the favicon route

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Rewrite the allowed_hosts comprehension under a fresh loop variable and call the Host check fixed, without noticing the tuple it builds is already identical to the parent's.
